findings.quote: uneventful
findings.note: ARGUABLE (not a double-key): 'The moment they describe is seldom uneventful' is grammatical and draws support from the same evidence the key uses - 'That is not the language of a comfortable ritual but of something with stakes' and 'a half-second in which force, timing and attention are all being read at once'. A candidate could argue that a moment 'with stakes' is by definition not uneventful. The key still wins on two counts: the disambiguator 'That is not the language of a comfortable ritual' points at freedom-from-worry (untroubled), not at incident-density, and 'uneventful' idiomatically qualifies stretches of time (an uneventful week/journey) rather than a half-second. Beatable on a skeptical reading, so flag rather than kill; adjudication may still want the distractor softened.

findings.quote: put both past a panel that is never told which is which
findings.note: class 3: collocation — the established idiom for submitting something for judgement is 'run something past someone'; 'put ... past' primarily lives in the fixed phrase 'wouldn't put it past him', so an editor would pause here. Editor's rewrite: 'run both past a panel that is never told which is which'. No other conviction: British spelling (grey, kilometres, neighbouring) is consistent, articles/agreement/tense are sound, and the texture (named chemist, dated relinings, pan counts, dry closing cadence) reads as edited magazine prose.

findings.quote: put both past a panel that is never told which is which
findings.note: class 3: collocation stretch. English submits samples 'before' a panel or 'runs' them 'past' someone; 'put X past Y' is idiomatically locked into 'I wouldn't put it past him', a different sense, so the phrasing briefly misfires. Editor's rewrite: 'put both before a panel that is never told which is which'.

findings.quote: I nybyggda villaområden flaggades det på fler dagar än tolv år tidigare, medan äldre bebyggelse låg still.
findings.note: Question style: q1 option B is a near-verbatim lift of the passage sentence (only the year '2023' removed), so the item is answerable by string-matching rather than by reading. HP LÄS options sit in paraphrase register — cf. var-2015-verb2-LÄS-016, where the keyed option 'Engelskan hotar svenskan mindre än svenskan hotar minoritetsspråken' restates the argument in wholly new wording, and var-2019-verb1-LÄS-018, whose options are invented examples rather than passage strings. Passage itself is fully authentic in genre and temperature; this is an option-register edge case for adjudication, not a genre failure.

findings.quote: I Gävle håller tatueraren Rolf Tvede en pärm med motiv han inte längre får frågor om.
findings.note: class 2/6: 'hålla en pärm' reads as an English 'keeps a binder' calque; Swedish keeps records with 'föra' (the very next sentence correctly has 'Han har fört den sedan nittiotalet'), so the collocation clashes with the author's own usage. Native alternative: 'för tatueraren Rolf Tvede en pärm ...' or 'har ... en pärm'.

findings.quote: av att någon har det på sin arbetsbeskrivning att gå ut klockan åtta
findings.note: class 2: preposition calqued from English 'on his job description'. A duty stands or is included IN the document in Swedish: 'står i arbetsbeskrivningen' / 'ingår i arbetsuppgifterna'. Native alternative: 'att någon har det i sin arbetsbeskrivning att gå ut klockan åtta'.

findings.quote: Den är vad som blir kvar när ingen längre har uppgiften.
findings.note: class 2: free relative 'vad som' in predicative position mirrors English 'it is what remains'; edited Swedish sakprosa prefers 'det som' here. Native alternative: 'Den är det som blir kvar när ingen längre har uppgiften.'

findings.quote: Fler dagar på en lista som ingen verkställer ger fler dagar som inte märks.
findings.note: class 6: collocation miss — man verkställer beslut, domar eller planer, inte en lista. Native alternative: 'en lista som ingen följer/omsätter i handling'.

findings.quote: Murar med skilda markslag på sina två sidor tycks hysa fler arter i kanten
findings.note: class 6: 'på sina två sidor' is an off-collocation for a wall's flanks and reads like a literal rendering of 'on its two sides'; the passage itself uses 'på sina båda sidor'. Native alternative: 'på var sin sida' / 'på sina båda sidor'.

findings.quote: att de inte är artrikare än snittet
findings.note: class 5: 'snittet' is sports/journalese shorthand inside otherwise high-register edited sakprosa ('härad', 'skavanker', 'åldersmärken'). Native alternative: 'än genomsnittet'.

findings.quote: I Gävle håller tatueraren Rolf Tvede en pärm med motiv han inte längre får frågor om.
findings.note: class 2/6: 'hålla en pärm' for maintaining a record is an English 'keeps a binder' collocation; Swedish maintains records with 'föra' (as the very next sentence does: 'Han har fört den sedan nittiotalet'), so the verb choice also clashes with the author's own usage. Grammatical, hence major not lethal. Native alternative: 'för tatueraren Rolf Tvede en pärm' or 'har ... en pärm'.

findings.quote: har det på sin arbetsbeskrivning att gå ut klockan åtta
findings.note: class 6: an 'arbetsbeskrivning' is a document, so Swedish puts duties 'i' it ('det står i hans arbetsbeskrivning'); 'på' patterns with lists/schedules and reads slightly off here. Native alternative: 'har det i sin arbetsbeskrivning'.

findings.quote: medan äldre bebyggelse låg still
findings.note: class 6: for a statistic that does not move, the idiom is 'ligga stilla' — which the same passage uses two paragraphs earlier ('andelen låg i stort sett stilla'); 'låg still' reads as physical motionlessness. Native alternative: 'låg stilla'.

findings.quote: och att de inte är artrikare än snittet
findings.note: class 5/6: 'snittet' for 'genomsnittet' is dictionary-marked colloquial (vard.) and sits inside an otherwise edited-sakprosa summary of a research finding; a copy editor would raise it. Native alternative: 'artrikare än genomsnittet'.

findings.quote: I Gävle håller tatueraren Rolf Tvede en pärm med motiv han inte längre får frågor om.
findings.note: class 2/6: 'håller en pärm' is a collocation miss that reads as the English 'keeps a binder'; Swedish 'hålla' does not take a document/record as object (one 'har' or 'för' a pärm/förteckning). The passage uses the correct verb two sentences later ('Han har fört den sedan nittiotalet'), which exposes the slip. Native alternative: 'I Gävle har tatueraren Rolf Tvede en pärm ...'.

findings.quote: medan äldre bebyggelse låg still
findings.note: class 1/4: 'still' is not a Swedish adverb form — the invariable word is 'stilla' ('ligga stilla'). The same passage writes it correctly one paragraph earlier ('medan andelen låg i stort sett stilla'), so this is a wrong form, not a stylistic variant, and it recurs verbatim in option 1B, propagating the error into student-visible text. No standalone Swedish 'still' occurs anywhere in the 27-exam authentic corpus (all 53 hits are English/ELF). Native alternative: 'medan äldre bebyggelse låg stilla'.

findings.quote: av att någon har det på sin arbetsbeskrivning att gå ut klockan åtta
findings.note: class 6: preposition/collocation miss — in Swedish a duty stands 'i' a job description ('det står i hens arbetsbeskrivning', 'ha i sin arbetsbeskrivning'); 'på sin arbetsbeskrivning' mirrors English 'on their job description'. The same sentence pair uses 'i' correctly for the budget line ('en rad i driftbudgeten'). Native alternative: 'har det i sin arbetsbeskrivning'.

findings.quote: That the usual load-path account is one the collection's own tests could not confirm.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick D, moderate confidence). Domain knowledge of the square-window fatigue story - stress concentration at the corners of pressurised cabin windows - makes 'the usual load-path account' identifiable, and a text framed around a collection's own rigs failing to reproduce it is a recognisable revisionist move. A is separately eliminable from form alone as the sole absolute ('will always fail sooner'). But C remains a substantive rival position (rounded corners as tolerance for rough shop-floor work) and B a substantive detail claim, so the passage still decides between them. No recall component and no form-alone determination.

findings.quote: Staling as a rearrangement of water inside a loaf rather than a loss from it.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick B, high confidence). That staling is starch retrogradation plus moisture migration from crumb to crust, rather than the loaf simply drying out, is textbook food science, so a domain-aware solver picks B on a 'mainly about' stem without reading anything. Form adds a weaker pull: A ('the trick of keeping a crust crisp') and D ('the reason a stale loaf can be freshened') are narrow single phenomena while B is the only general thesis, and B partially subsumes D - though not the whole option set, so the containment tell is incomplete. C is a substantive alternative framing of the same material. Normal main-idea design with a globally true key, routed to adjudication rather than killed.

findings.quote: Murar med skilda markslag på sina två sidor tycks hysa fler arter i kanten, men bara på solbelysta sträckor.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick B). The ecotone / edge-effect principle - a boundary between two unlike habitats carries more species than a boundary inside one - is standard ecology and points at the 'skilda markslag' family (B/C) over A. C is then eliminable from form alone as the unqualified twin of B ('varje mur i häradet, oberoende av hur den ligger i terrängen'), leaving the correctly scoped member. A and D remain substantive alternative findings, and a correctly scoped key beside an over-scoped twin is standard authentic HP construction, so this is domain knowledge plus one overclaim elimination, not a form-alone leak.

findings.quote: Att ett material på tvåhundra murar är alldeles för litet för att något samband över huvud taget ska kunna prövas.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick A). Two options fall without the passage: B is an absolute overclaim - two hundred walls is an ample material, and 'för att något samband över huvud taget ska kunna prövas' is a claim no competent critic makes - and D drifts to a different indicator (lavflora and air pollution) that the stem's 'invändning mot Ekelins tolkning' does not engage. That leaves A and C, with A further favoured as the only option offering a rival explanation of the finding, which is what an objection to a tolkning idiomatically targets. C (selection bias from owner permission) stays substantive, and the stem-fit pull is a preference rather than an entailment, so the passage still decides.

findings.quote: Ekelins och Frejmarks förklaringar utesluter varandra, och materialet visar att det är Frejmark som har rätt.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick C). B is eliminable from form alone as a double overclaim - mutual exclusivity plus an adjudication of the dispute, which an expository text presenting two live positions essentially never delivers. D is eliminable as a bare factual detail about why the walls were built, the wrong shape for a 'överensstämmer bäst med texten' synthesis stem. That leaves A and C, and C is the nuanced option ('men ... ligger utanför skyddets räckvidd och är dessutom omtvistat') against A's evaluative overreach about cultural-heritage worth. A remains a substantive reading and a nuanced key beside overclaiming distractors is ordinary HP design, so this is partial blind elimination, not a lethal cluster tell.

findings.quote: Andelen som ombads förklara sina motiv sjönk lika kraftigt oavsett var på kroppen tatueringen satt.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick C, low-to-moderate confidence). No world knowledge bears on a fictional interview study, but form narrows it. C and D are an explicit pair on a single axis - a decline confined to certain body sites versus one that fell 'lika kraftigt oavsett var på kroppen' - which marks that axis as the one the item turns on and pushes A and B aside; A additionally reads as a causal reframing rather than a reported result. Between the pair the qualified member C is the test-wise pick. D is a perfectly reportable uniform finding and not filler, so this is an edge above chance, not a determination.

findings.quote: Det som verkligen visar att tatueringen normaliserats är ointresset, och samtidigt går något av motivets innebörd förlorat.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick B, high confidence) - the closest call in this set and the one worth adjudicator attention. Three options are disqualifiable without the text: A is an absolute ('det avgörande beviset', 'normaliseringen är genomförd'), C proposes that the intrusive curiosity would be worth restoring, a stance a columnist is unlikely to hold, and D denies any determinable change, which sits against the stem's presupposition that the författare 'anser' something about the normalisation. B is left as the only balanced concessive option, the characteristic shape of an author-attitude key. Held at flag rather than kill because D is itself hedged, so the 'only hedged option among absolutes' tell does not strictly hold, and A/C/D are substantive stances rather than filler.

findings.quote: Ökningen i villaområdena beror på att kommunerna där hade slutat flagga, vilket fick de boende i området att ta över.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick B). C falls from form alone as a causal overclaim that survey material of this kind cannot support, and D as a magnitude claim of the same overreaching shape ('så stor att den vägde upp bortfallet'). That leaves A and B as the two readings of one axis - a uniform rise 'oavsett hur gammal bebyggelsen' versus a rise confined to newly built villa areas - and the qualified member B is the test-wise pick. A is a normal survey outcome and not filler, so this is two eliminations plus a hedging heuristic, not a form-alone determination.

findings.quote: Ansvaret för att dagarna märks bör flyttas från fastighetsägarna till den myndighet som fastställer listan.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick D). C is eliminable on stem fit - it is a counter-proposal about where responsibility should sit, not an 'invändning ... mot förslaget' - and B concedes the proposal is 'i sak välmotiverat', making it an objection to timing rather than to the förslag itself. That leaves A and D, with D the pointed 'the list is not the problem' move an argumentative column characteristically makes. A (the traditionalist dilution argument) remains a substantive objection, so the passage is still needed to decide.

findings.quote: The change showed up in how the pans had to be read, rather than in the salt that came off them.
findings.note: Clean stems-only run: no passage, key, rationale or _seed in context (supersedes the earlier contaminated record for this candidate). PARTIALLY (blind pick B, moderate confidence). The setting is invented (Aveste, Pella Marsa), so no world knowledge bears on it; the edge is option-archetype only. Two options fall without the passage: A closes on a prescriptive leap ('the choice of floor can now be made on cost alone'), which an 'implied' stem essentially never keys, and D asserts a measured quantity (faster edge drying -> more magnesium in the crust), the shape of a stated finding rather than an implication. That leaves B, the not-X-but-Y reframe, against C ('leave it unclear whether pans floored in concrete can meet the mark at all'), which is a live and substantive outcome for a two-season trial. B vs C is not decidable from form - the passage must supply whether the concrete changed the salt, the reading of the pans, or the mark's standing. No recall component and no lethal cluster tell.

findings.quote: The writer allows that the objection is a fair one, and still does not let it close the argument.
findings.note: Clean stems-only run: no passage, key, rationale or _seed in context (supersedes the earlier contaminated record for this candidate). PARTIALLY (blind pick C, moderate confidence). Author-attitude stem carrying the usual concessive-balance cue: A is one-directional adoption of Panek's position ('leaves the craft question there') and B is one-directional imputation of bad faith to a committee, a stance an expository writer rarely takes as his own, so a test-wise reader with zero domain knowledge downweights both and works inside the two-sided pair. The tell is explicitly NOT a clean 3-1 cluster: D ('largely answered by Solbes, with only the inspector's unannounced visit left as a difficulty') is also concessive and a substantive rival, and deciding C against D requires knowing from the passage how far Solbes actually met the objection. Materially better than chance from form, not decided by it.

findings.quote: A protected method guards what an inspector can see, while the salt turns on a judgement nobody records.
findings.note: Clean stems-only run: no passage, key, rationale or _seed in context (supersedes the earlier contaminated record for this candidate). PARTIALLY (blind pick B, moderate-to-high confidence). Main-idea stem where three options are single-direction claims built on overreach verbs - A 'overturned ... faith' and pinned to 'one chemist', C 'would not otherwise outlast mechanised production', D 'spoils ... chemistry cannot explain' - while B is the measured two-clause synthesis naming both halves of a tension. That asymmetry is visible from form alone and is a documented main-idea test-wiseness cue, letting A and C go blind. Held at flag rather than kill because D is a coherent alternative thesis for a piece involving tasting panels, and B's actual content (inspector-visible rules versus an unrecorded judgement) cannot be confirmed as the text's through-line without the passage.
